analysis: The code calls Method.invoke() to call a static method removeInstance on a class loaded via Class.forName. The javadoc lists several exceptions. For each: IllegalAccessException - not avoided because the method's accessibility is unknown; IllegalArgumentException - avoided because the method signature is matched exactly and argument types are correct; InvocationTargetException - not avoided because the underlying method may throw an exception; NullPointerException - avoided because the method is static, so null object argument is ignored; ExceptionInInitializerError - avoided because the class is initialized by Class.forName before the invoke call. Also note that NoSuchMethodException from getDeclaredMethod is caught by the generic Exception catch but is not an invoke exception.
answer: IllegalAccessException: not avoided. IllegalArgumentException: avoided. InvocationTargetException: not avoided. NullPointerException: avoided. ExceptionInInitializerError: avoided.
remark: IllegalAccessException can be thrown if the removeInstance method is not accessible (e.g., private or protected) because setAccessible is not called. InvocationTargetException is thrown if the underlying removeInstance method throws any exception during its execution.
